description: Leaving is easier than returning. A person who goes abroad to study or work may find the residency they left with no longer recognised on the way back.
energy_note: The exit is free. The return is the application.
notes: Directly parallel to RET-001 in assets/text/iran.

aspect: Refusal happens at the border, where there is no lawyer
description: The decision is taken at a crossing, by an official, in minutes, with no written reasons and no counsel present. Challenging it afterwards means doing so from another country.
money_note: Legal costs of a challenge mounted from abroad.
energy_note: Litigating your way home from a hotel.

aspect: It changes what going abroad means
description: Studying overseas stops being an opportunity and becomes a gamble against your own residency. Many decline scholarships for exactly this reason.
energy_note: A degree, against the risk of the door closing.

description: Four years in Leipzig. She is careful: she visits every eighteen months, keeps utility bills, keeps the flat in her mother's name. At the bridge in the fifth year, a man in his twenties looks at a screen and says the centre of her life appears to be in Germany.
money_note: The value of a residency lost.
energy_note: A doctorate, traded for a city.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the returnee camps excluded from the count
description: OCHA's obstacle count explicitly excludes the closure of Jenin and Tulkarm refugee camps for returnees - meaning people barred from re-entering their own camp do not appear in the headline figure for movement restrictions at all.
energy_note: Barred from your own camp, and not counted as restricted.
